resources.string: Above 70 = overbought (run up a lot), below 30 = oversold (fallen a lot) • 50–70 = rising, but not too much
How far the MACD line sits above (+) or below (-) its signal line, as % of the price • above 0% = rising
How many days ago the MACD crossed its signal line from below • up to \"3 days ago\" = a fresh bullish crossover; stocks below the signal drop out

Both come from each stock\'s 6 months of daily prices, as on charting sites. RSI (14) runs from 0 to 100: above 70 is overbought (run up a lot), below 30 oversold (fallen a lot), 50–70 rising. MACD (12, 26, 9): the gap between the 12- and 26-day exponential averages, and its 9-day signal line. MACD above its signal = rising; the day it crosses the signal from below is a bullish crossover. The Filters have all three: an RSI range, how far MACD sits above or below its signal (as % of the price), and how many days ago the crossover came (up to \"3 days ago\" = a fresh crossover). The stock\'s detail shows today\'s value of both. In a live market, today\'s moving price counts too.
